Primary proposition.statement='For the real mean-zero periodic equation U_t=U*U_x+U_xxx on ℝ/(2*pi*ℤ), use hat U(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral U(x)exp(-i*k*x)dx, ||U||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2s)|hat U(k)|^2, and z_k(t)=exp(i*k^3*t)hat U(t)(k). For every s>0 and horizon Q>0, every initial datum U_0 in dot H^s has a distributional solution with z in C([0,Q];dot H^s), unique in the source solution class (z in L^infinity dot H^0 satisfying z_k(t)-z_k(0)=(i*k/2)integral_0^t sum_(k1+k2=k)exp(i*3*k*k1*k2*r)z_k1(r)z_k2(r)dr). Its dot H^0 norm is conserved, and the flow depends Lipschitz continuously on the initial data in dot H^s, uniformly on bounded dot H^s sets on [0,Q]. The Galerkin approximations (with the nonlinear inputs and output projected to |k|<=m and high coefficients frozen) have dot H^s bounds uniform in m, depending only on s,Q, the initial dot H^s norm and an upper bound for the initial dot H^0 norm. For 0<sigma<s they admit a subsequence converging strongly in L^q([0,Q];dot H^sigma), 1<q<infinity, and weak-* in L^infinity dot H^s to this solution; the same dot H^s bound holds for the limit. For s=0 there is a unique C([0,Q];dot H^0) solution, conserving that norm and depending Lipschitz continuously on its data.
